test: Build job-level material share: sum of material PO amounts per order job divided by the job's shipped value (shipment qty x SO unit_price, and separately invoice amount), grouped by shipment year 2016-2025. Split by material (carbon steel vs other), repeat vs first-time parts, and whether the part's unit_price changed vs its previous order. Compare uplift (invoice amount - qty x price) to the extra material share above the 2016-2020 baseline. Check lag between PO ordered_on and shipment to separate timing from margin.
support: Job-level material share rises in 2021-2023 vs 2016-2020 (not just GL), the rise concentrates on carbon-steel repeat parts with unchanged unit_price, and invoice uplift covers a small fraction of the extra material dollars.
weaken: Job-level share stays flat (GL gap is ordering timing), or repeat-part prices reset within 1-2 orders, or uplift covers most of the extra cost.
expect: Moderately confident (~65%) that job-level share rises in 2021-2022 for carbon steel, with lagging repeat prices; the dollar gap likely smaller than the GL-based $2.5-3M because of the 28.9% unreceived POs and order-timing effects.
